The Battle of Samtani was a tribal conflict fought between the Sindhi Pahnwar tribe and the Khosa Baloch tribe in Samtani, present-day Dadu, during the late 17th century. The battle ended in a decisive Sindhi victory, resulting in the death of the Khosa leader Sardar Gola Khosa.
Background
The Sindhi tribe of Pahnwar had long been established in Samtani, an area within present-day Dadu.  During the period of Mughal rule in Sindh, the Pahnwars are recorded as having carried out raids against Mughal authority and its local representatives. At this time, the Kalhoras functioned as nawabs of Sindh under Mughal patronage and were responsible for maintaining order in the region. In response to continued unrest, the Kalhoras settled members of the Khosa Baloch tribe in Samtani, likely with the intention of counterbalancing Pahnwar influence and securing control over the area. This settlement significantly altered local power relations and intensified tensions between the two tribes. The Pahnwars, viewing the Khosa presence as an encroachment on their traditional territory, organized armed resistance under their leader, Sardar Hyder Pahnwar. According to the Jangnama, this conflict culminated in a direct confrontation in which the Pahnwars attacked the Khosas, inflicted heavy losses upon them, and killed their leader, Sardar Gola Khosa.
Aftermath
Following their victory, the Pahnwars emerged as the dominant power in Dadu and maintained control of the region for a prolonged period. They also repelled raids by another Sindhi tribe, the Burfat, until the rise of Yar Muhammad Kalhoro, who after consolidating power over the Kalhora throne, overthrew the Pahnwars and took control of Dadu.
